title: Learned ultrasound analysis identifies heel-texture differences between clinical groups
summary: Learned segmentation and texture classifiers identified heel-pad ultrasound differences between 76 participants with diabetes and 47 controls. Recurrent wavelet-correlation features contributed to group separation, but the groups also differed in age and sex without adjustment. These are image-level group associations, not diabetes-specific tissue mechanisms or validated patient-level diagnosis.
ai_technology: H-SAM segmentation with LoRA; XGBoost and other classifiers; SHAP interpretation
organization: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology; Shanghai University of Medicine and Health Sciences; Fudan University; Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Shanghai Institute of Technology

source_review.scope: Read actual primary H-SAM training, participant-level partition, feature-selection/tuning Methods, final image-vector Results, recurrent-feature/SHAP findings and demographic limitations. Original canonical primary online date November 5 is distinguished from index-filled November 1. Writing-assistance disclosures are not counted as the enabling AI role. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Single-center study of 123 participants and 289 heel-pad ultrasound images. H-SAM segmented two tissue layers; wavelet/texture features underwent training-only statistical screening and grouped feature selection. Seven classifiers shared participant-disjoint partitions. The final XGBoost model evaluated 45 image-derived vectors from 18 held-out participants, with AUC 0.9407. Six features recurred across classifiers; macrochamber wavelet-correlation features showed consistent model contribution patterns.
evidence.unknown: Patients were older than controls (median 61 versus 49 years), and sex distributions differed; no adjusted analyses isolated diabetes effects. Multiple image vectors per participant define the reported AUC, not independent participant-level diagnosis. Single device/center, segmentation uncertainty and incomplete diabetes/PAD characterization limit interpretation. No histological, biomechanical or causal tissue mechanism, clinical benefit or independent cohort replication was established.
evidence.ai_role: H-SAM learned segmentation produced layer masks; learned classifiers and feature-attribution analyses identified texture descriptors that consistently separated the sampled clinical groups.
